trails.title: Toybox User Manual
trails.description: After all, you may not even know how to play with toys at all!

content.text:
Step 1: Swear you are more than six years old or at least no longer have a habit of putting toys in your mouth.

Step 2: Place the toybox upright on a firm surface, with my handsome faces facing up.

Step 3: Make sure no cats are around.

Step 4: Make sure you have at least one friend to play with—multiple personalities count as friends too!

Step 5: Chant this happy little incantation: "With arcanum comes endless imagination! The Musae Museum, right before your eyes!"

Musae III reserves the right to final interpretation of this product.

trails.title: Aftermath
trails.description: The internet is less reliable than you think.

content.text:
0001 Anonymous No.00000001 ▶
The "language disorder" badly damaged our servers. Much of our historical data was corrupted into garbled text and couldn't be recovered. There was nothing I could do except format the servers.

0002 Anonymous No.00000012 ▶
So this is what wanting to turn back time feels like ... I almost want to join Manus Vindictae.

0003 Anonymous No.00000038 ▶>>00000043
Whatever. A whole year's worth of my experimental data got turned into gibberish. How could things get any worse?

0004 Anonymous No.00000043 ▶
>>00000038
Becoming Enigma.

0005 Anonymous No.00000056 ▶>>00000067
What if we throw all the servers into the "Storm"? How likely are we to get a server from before the "language disorder"?

0006 Anonymous No.00000067 ▶
>>00000056
The data says the chance is so small that even an astronomer would ignore it. But if we made the "Storm" affect all of Laplace ...

0007 Anonymous No.00000073 ▶
Someone's evil index has surpassed Medicine Pocket's. I've contacted security.

0008 Anonymous No.00000081 ▶>>00000083
What a disaster. You know, one hexadecimal John Titor is already enough trouble.

0009 Anonymous No.00000083 ▶>>00000090
>>00000081
I heard she spoke almost only English the whole time during the "language disorder."

0010 Anonymous No.00000090 ▶>>00000113
>>00000083
What?! Sweet Madam Lucy! Did that really happen?

0011 Anonymous No.00000113 ▶>>00000125
>>00000090
Maybe. Maybe not. Rumors about her are always like that.

0012 Anonymous No.00000125 ▶
>>00000113
I'd like to join Manus Vindictae too. It's honestly worth considering.

0013 Anonymous No.00000128 ▶
That's it, folks. Laplace is done for.

items.text: There must be a theory that unifies everything in the universe.
Because every puzzle has a solution.
Lines form a framework, waiting for one letter to anchor the answer.
The world is like a crossword. If you follow the clues—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ugh.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Damn it. Isn't it about time humanity evolved beyond sleep?
He shakes his head and fixes his gaze on the jumbled grid lines covering his desk.
Pushing the papers and files aside, he turns on the screen.
3 PM.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's only been six hours. Looks like the little biter's actually done some work in between destroying public property. Side effects have certainly lessened.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Did I throw away the instruction manual? What did it say?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Never mind. The lethal side effects have already been eliminated; the other symptoms don't matter.
He rummages under the papers for the metal tube and tips two colorful candies into his palm.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I hope this helps.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Toybox research, the Timekeeper's request, new results ... and Lorentz. Alright.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As always, problems rarely come alone.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But the more problems there are, the closer we are to the solution.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We need to stop creating more problems!
Ulrich slams his fist down on the desk in an attempt to end the chaotic discussion spiraling before him.
Unfortunately, in Laplace, shouting only invites a louder rebuttal.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Then get rid of the approval system so we can all work in peace for a couple weeks! You know, spend our time actually experimenting instead of writing damn reports!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: That's our problem! I'm telling you, even if Enigma locked himself in that room for the next decade, he wouldn't get through them all!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Focus on the matter at hand, Researcher Medicine Pocket!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The toybox has been fixed for now, and the communication problems it caused have also disappeared. But we need to come up with a way to prevent any similar incidents in the future.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: And it's crucial we figure out how it had such a widespread effect. We can't risk almost all of Laplace speaking in cipher again.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I, for one, believe it's related to the Storm Syndrome. But our research progress has been far too slow, so I need everyone—

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: There you go again. You're gonna say that the "language disorder" interfered with our work, right?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Well, let me make this clear: whether I use cipher or decimal or freaking latte art to communicate, it's not gonna stop me from doing what I want.
Medicine Pocket mimics Ulrich's tone, drawing out the words.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Those emergency handbooks are only filling that tank of yours with useless, garbage data. Whatever happens, my advice is the same—

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Mind your own business and let us fend for ourselves!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Hah, sounds like you've gotten over accidentally ordering Critter chow at the canteen. I suppose it is quite difficult to decipher a Tetris-based language, no?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And no, we can't just "blow up the toybox," Medicine Pocket. As I said before, it cannot be destroyed through arcane nor scientific means. You should know when to quit.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Blow it up? Absolutely not!
The ferrofluid nearly bounces in the tank.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Adler already notified us that the Foundation is pressuring us to deliver persuasive research results!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This isn't the first time they've used our "laissez-faire attitude" as an excuse to attack Laplace. We need to use the toybox's simulations to create a reliable emergency protocol!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Okay, I get you. We just need to submit something that'll shut them up.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: So, why don't you round up everyone who's been wasting research materials, hand them all "Lorentz" ID badges, and turn them over?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I did hear the Foundation has been quite "lively" lately. As crowded and chaotic as the crystal structure of austenite, supposedly.
Ulrich is clearly trying his best to hold it together. Eventually, the tremor in his voice module settles.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: That's quite enough. Now, if you'd please return to today's topic.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Researcher Pointer, Researcher X. How are the results of your data analysis?
The two researchers have long grown accustomed to the lab's clamor. They know silence is the best way to keep out of it.
Pointer pushes a stack of files toward Ulrich.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Here's my section. I've included a summary for the Timekeeper's perusal.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: In simple terms, the "Flood" has altered the characteristics of the "Storm."

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: The vast majority of our past data has been rendered useless. Our most reliable models require multiple rounds of verification. Therefore, our current conclusions are for reference only.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This should be plenty. I'm confident we'll adapt to these new conditions very soon.
Everyone silently agrees.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Have we made any discoveries regarding the arcane fluctuations emanating from the toybox?

items.speaker: X
items.text: If we're only looking at the numbers, the magnitude of these arcane fluctuations far exceeds normal levels.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I also consulted all the arcanists I know with arcane skills related to language, words, or sound. None of them could find any manmade traces in the fluctuations.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I have two hypotheses. One: This toybox is a naturally occurring arcane object. And two: Its core holds a power beyond most arcanists' comprehension.
He pauses. Hesitation, perhaps?

items.speaker: X
items.text: I also have a personal theory. Mr. Ludwig's arcane fluctuations ...
Thud!
The meeting room door is thrown open, slamming it against the wall.
Everyone turns toward the figure that has just burst in.
Mr. Enigma.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Door's unlocked.
The visitor pushes the door open and enters.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I already reviewed your application last Wednesday, X.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And you and Hissabeth can stop submitting those clinical trial applications for Medicine Pocket's project.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Oh, I have a friend ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Regulus is not an option, either. There isn't a hair on her body that doesn't scream "arcanist."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I will handle this myself. After all, I was the one who questioned Medicine Pocket on the possibility of resuming research on the topic in the first place.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's a compelling research direction. An antidote for Picrasma extract suitable for human consumption and a universally applicable, edible extract with energizing effects.
He delivers the long string of terms with neither a stumble nor a pause, as if reciting from a script.

items.speaker: X
items.text: There's no need for you to worry. I read the project proposal. Medicine Pocket already consulted me on a few issues.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That proposal was supposed to be confidential. *sigh* Never mind, but we need to act like this research topic doesn't exist until it yields some results.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You are all pureblood arcanists. You have a natural tolerance for Picrasma extract. But it's simply too dangerous to move straight on to pureblood humans.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Well, I suppose it's about time my quarter-arcanist blood came in handy.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I understand, Mr. Enigma. I have no intention—nor the power, mind you—to interfere with anyone's decision.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But I did receive a document I think you should see.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Of course you did. There's always more.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's about the "language disorder" caused by the toybox's malfunction. I'm sure you're familiar with it.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Although the world outside has returned to normal, a lot of curious occurrences have appeared in the toybox. Allegedly, the behavior of its inhabitants has been becoming increasingly formulaic and unified.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Of course, these are Mr. Ulrich's words. I haven't seen it for myself.

items.speaker: X
items.text: The specifics are on top.
He hands over the document.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I read the whole thing. It's comprehensive. Exhaustive, even. It should be more than enough to submit to the Foundation.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But Ulrich isn't convinced it's persuasive enough, so he hasn't turned it in.

items.speaker: X
items.text: We all know how easy it is to fall down a research rabbit hole. He needs someone on the outside to step in and make a decision.

items.speaker: X
items.text: At least, that's what I think.

items.speaker: X
items.text: There's also the small matter of a waveform contaminating the toybox's arcane fluctuations—a waveform extremely similar to that of our dear Mr. Raven.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I've compared it. It's distinctly different from the other simulation data.
X delivers the last of his prepared lines.
And with that, the butterfly has flapped its wings.
He steps out and shuts the door behind him.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ulrich!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm trying to return this copy of your report that you "forgot."
